NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager who has always wet the rope before tying it, on advice from a stranger, passes the same advice on.

setup.name: The scene
setup.text: Years ago, when (name1) was learning to build, a villager (he/she) barely knew walked past and said, "Wet the rope before you tie it. It shrinks tight when it dries." Then they walked on. That was all. (name1) doesn't remember their face any more, or even what season it was. But every single day since, (he/she) has wet the rope before tying it, and every single knot (he/she) has tied has held. Today (he/she) catches (him/her)self saying it to a young villager on the path: "Wet the rope first. It shrinks tight when it dries." Then (he/she) walks on. Maybe the young villager will remember it. Maybe not. (name1) hopes so. It was the best advice (he/she) ever got, and it took about two breaths to give.
